story_description: Create the foundational data model, builder logic, and view model for representing hook execution events in a timeline/Gantt chart format, enabling visualization of hook lifecycles with proper temporal relationships, hierarchical structure, and real-time updates.
task_description: Create the HookGanttViewModel ObservableObject that manages timeline state, coordinates data fetching from HookStore, handles view mode switching between turn and session views, tracks expand/collapse state, computes derived metrics (time range, duration, hook count), and subscribes to real-time hook execution updates.
atom_description: Implement HookGanttViewModel as a MainActor-isolated ObservableObject with published properties for viewMode (HookGanttViewMode enum), timelineEvents array, selectedEvent optional, expandedEventIds set, and isLoading state. Add computed properties for timeRange, totalDuration, and hookCount. Implement data loading from HookStore, real-time observation via Combine publishers, and expand/collapse toggle methods.
problem_statement: The Gantt visualization requires a reactive state management layer that bridges the data model (HookTimelineEvent from G001) and builder logic (HookTimelineBuilder from G002) with the SwiftUI views (G004-G007). Without a dedicated ViewModel, views would need to manage complex state like expand/collapse tracking, mode switching, real-time subscriptions, and derived metric calculations directly, violating separation of concerns and making the UI code unmaintainable.

FR9: totalDuration computed property shall sum durations of root-level events (depth 0) returning TimeInterval

implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookGanttViewModel.swift in Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Define HookGanttViewMode enum with cases turn, session and RawRepresentable conformance for String
Step 3: Define @MainActor class HookGanttViewModel: ObservableObject with private let hookStore: HookStore and private let sessionId: UUID? stored properties
Step 4: Add @Published var viewMode: HookGanttViewMode = .turn
Step 5: Add @Published var timelineEvents: [HookTimelineEvent] = []
Step 6: Add @Published var selectedEvent: HookTimelineEvent? = nil
Step 7: Add @Published var expandedEventIds: Set<UUID> = []
Step 8: Add @Published var isLoading: Bool = false
Step 9: Add private var cancellables: Set<AnyCancellable> = [] for Combine subscription storage
Step 10: Add computed property timeRange: ClosedRange<Date> that finds min startTime and max endTime from all events, returning sensible default if empty
Step 11: Add computed property totalDuration: TimeInterval that sums root events durations using compactMap and reduce
Step 12: Add computed property hookCount: Int with recursive helper function to count events at all depths
Step 13: Add init(hookStore: HookStore, sessionId: UUID? = nil) initializer storing dependencies
Step 14: Add func loadTimeline() async that sets isLoading true, fetches executions, builds timeline via builder, updates timelineEvents, sets isLoading false
Step 15: Add func toggleExpanded(eventId: UUID) that uses Set insert/remove based on contains check
Step 16: Add func selectEvent(_ event: HookTimelineEvent?) that assigns to selectedEvent
Step 17: Add func switchMode(to mode: HookGanttViewMode) that updates viewMode, nils selectedEvent, calls Task { await loadTimeline() }
Step 18: Add func startObserving() that subscribes to HookRunner.shared.executionPublisher with sink calling handleNewExecution
Step 19: Add func stopObserving() that calls cancellables.removeAll()
Step 20: Add private func handleNewExecution(_ execution: HookExecution) that creates event via factory method and inserts into timelineEvents
Step 21: Add deinit that calls stopObserving() to prevent leaks
Step 22: Add documentation comments for all public API
Step 23: Write unit tests covering all public methods and computed properties

ui_states: Empty state: timelineEvents is empty array, hookCount is 0, show empty placeholder in view
Loading state: isLoading is true, view shows progress indicator
Loaded state: isLoading is false, timelineEvents populated, view renders Gantt rows
Turn mode: viewMode is .turn, timeline shows hooks from current/selected turn only
Session mode: viewMode is .session, timeline shows all turns with nested hooks
Collapsed row: eventId not in expandedEventIds, children hidden in view
Expanded row: eventId in expandedEventIds, children visible in view
Selected event: selectedEvent is non-nil, view highlights corresponding bar and shows detail panel
No selection: selectedEvent is nil, no highlight or detail panel
ui_interactions: View mode toggle: User taps segment control, view calls switchMode(to:), ViewModel reloads timeline
Row expand/collapse: User taps chevron, view calls toggleExpanded(eventId:), ViewModel updates set, view re-renders children
Event selection: User taps bar, view calls selectEvent(_:), ViewModel updates selectedEvent, view shows detail
Real-time update: HookRunner emits execution, ViewModel receives via subscription, updates timelineEvents, view animates new bar
Load on appear: View appears, calls loadTimeline(), ViewModel fetches data, view transitions from loading to loaded
edge_cases: Edge case 1: No hook executions exist for session - timelineEvents empty, timeRange returns Date() to Date() (empty closed range), totalDuration returns 0, hookCount returns 0
Edge case 2: Session ID is nil - load all executions across all sessions (global view)
Edge case 3: HookStore.getExecutions throws error - catch and set timelineEvents to empty, log error, do not crash
Edge case 4: switchMode called while loadTimeline is in progress - should cancel previous load or queue (use Task cancellation)
Edge case 5: toggleExpanded called for non-existent eventId - no-op, Set handles gracefully
Edge case 6: selectEvent called with event not in timelineEvents - still set selectedEvent (view handles mismatch)
Edge case 7: Real-time execution arrives for different session than current sessionId filter - ignore if sessionId filter is active
Edge case 8: startObserving called multiple times - should not create duplicate subscriptions (check cancellables.isEmpty or use single subscription)
Edge case 9: stopObserving called when no subscriptions exist - no-op, cancellables.removeAll() is safe on empty set
Edge case 10: deinit called while async loadTimeline is in progress - Task should be cancelled to prevent accessing deallocated self
failure_modes: FM1: HookStore.getExecutions fails (database error, corruption) - catch error, log with OSLog, set timelineEvents to empty, optionally surface error to user via separate @Published error property
FM2: HookTimelineBuilder returns empty array for non-empty executions (bug in builder) - timeline appears empty, user confusion, should log warning if executions.count > 0 but events.count == 0
FM3: Combine subscription to HookRunner never emits (publisher not firing) - real-time updates do not appear, user must manually refresh, fallback: add pull-to-refresh or periodic polling
FM4: Memory pressure from very large timeline (10000+ events) - timelineEvents array grows unbounded, recommend pagination or virtualization in view layer, ViewModel should expose slice accessors
FM5: Main actor deadlock from nested async calls - ensure all async work uses Task {} not blocking await on main, use nonisolated helpers for CPU work
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/HookGanttViewModel.swift. Remove executionPublisher addition from HookRunner if added solely for this feature. Views depending on ViewModel will fail to compile, remove those references. No data migration needed as ViewModel holds ephemeral state only.

risks: Risk 1: MainActor isolation may cause unexpected deadlocks if async helpers are not properly nonisolated
Risk 2: Combine subscription may leak if deinit is not called (e.g., ViewModel held by closure)
Risk 3: Real-time updates may cause UI jank if handleNewExecution triggers expensive rebuilds
Risk 4: Large timeline (1000+ events) may cause memory pressure and slow computed properties
Risk 5: Dependency on HookRunner modification could block implementation if HookRunner changes are delayed
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Use Task {} for async work instead of blocking await; mark CPU-intensive helpers as nonisolated
Mitigation 2: Store ViewModel in @StateObject to ensure proper lifecycle; audit for closure captures
Mitigation 3: Batch updates with Combine debounce/throttle if jank observed; profile with Instruments
Mitigation 4: Implement pagination or limit displayed events; cache computed property values
Mitigation 5: Implement ViewModel with mock publisher first; HookRunner modification is small (single property addition)
risk_register.blast_radius: Medium - ViewModel is central to Gantt feature. Failure breaks all Gantt views (G004-G007). Does not affect core hook execution, settings, or other UI. Contained to F007 feature scope.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If ViewModel proves problematic, simplify to non-reactive version that fetches on demand without real-time updates. Views can call loadTimeline() explicitly on appear and via manual refresh button. Remove Combine dependency for simpler implementation.
